final_candidates.decision_summary: Exhibits very high EVEscape immune escape potential (z=0.882) and top pLM plausibility among candidates. Disrupts key antibody contacts in the V3 region while preserving structural viability.

Demonstrates exceptional antibody escape predictions (z=0.895) in the crucial V1/V2 loop epitope region. Well-characterized in HIV-1 literature for conferring broad neutralizing antibody resistance while preserving envelope viral fitness.
Shows strong predicted immune escape (z=0.882) at the V1/V2 glycan apex. Disruption of this site effectively impairs antibody neutralization while maintaining functional folding.

stop_reason.detail: Top 3 candidates are robustly validated across escape phenotype and pLM feasibility metrics, establishing a clear lead over alternatives.

history.rationale: Disrupts the key V3 base N-glycan motif (N337-E338-T339) in BG505, promoting escape from PGT121-class broadly neutralizing antibodies while maintaining viral fitness.
High antibody escape score combined with the highest pLM sequence plausibility among candidates.
Maintains top rank due to strong EVEscape score and highest ESM-1v plausibility among top candidates.
Eliminates the conserved N275 glycosylation site near the CD4 binding site, conferring resistance to VRC01-class antibodies with minimal impact on envelope folding.
Moderate escape score but near-zero pLM plausibility.
Decent escape score, but low evolutionary tolerance.
Reverses charge in the V1V2 loop region, mediating immune escape from PG9/PG16-like quaternary antibodies while preserving entry function.
Highest predicted antibody escape score with moderate sequence plausibility.
High EVEscape score and highest Swiss-Prot MSA frequency among candidates, balancing low ESM-1v likelihood.
Disrupts the N151 glycan site in the V1V2 domain, reducing sensitivity to V1V2 glycan-directed neutralizers while preserving replication capability.
Strong predicted antibody escape combined with reasonable sequence plausibility.
Strong escape profile with moderate homolog frequency.
Removes the N384 glycosylation site near the CD4 binding site, facilitating antibody escape while maintaining structural stability.
Lowest overall combined support across escape and fitness dimensions.
Lowest overall combined support.
Knocks out the glycosylation sequon at N337 by substituting the +2 threonine, enabling escape from V3-glycan targeting antibodies.
Good sequence plausibility score alongside moderate escape prediction.
Solid backup option with good pLM score and decent EVEscape support.
Disrupts the N390 glycan sequon in the outer domain, altering antibody accessibility with low risk of destabilizing the core fold.
Moderate escape score offset by very low pLM score.
Good escape potential but weak evolutionary/pLM signals.
Modifies the V3 crown loop motif to alter turn flexibility and escape crown-directed antibodies while maintaining CD4 co-receptor engagement.
Weak escape prediction and poor pLM likelihood.
Reranked slightly higher due to notable evolutionary frequency in MSA.
Abolishes the N330 glycosylation motif, altering local epitope masking to escape specific neutralizers.
Lower escape potential and very low sequence plausibility.
Moderate escape signal with low sequence/MSA preference.
Directly removes the N330 glycan attachment residue, conferring escape from antibodies recognizing the high-mannose patch.
Moderate escape potential penalized by low sequence model likelihood.
Moderate escape score with low sequence likelihood.
